free_tier.stated: no sandbox-specific free allowance is published; sandbox compute bills through the same per-second Container Apps meters, whose first 180,000 vCPU-seconds and 360,000 GiB-seconds a month are free

limits.value: sandbox compute bills per second through the Container Apps meters
a stopped sandbox incurs no CPU or memory fee; a snapshot preserves memory and disk
creating or managing a sandbox requires the Container Apps SandboxGroup Data Owner role assignment

identity_cost.detail: A card and a phone number, because a sandbox bills through an Azure subscription. Azure's signup FAQ: 'All you need is a phone number, a credit card or a debit card (non-prepaid), and a Microsoft account or a GitHub account.' A second gate on the card: 'Only credit cards are accepted in Hong Kong and Brazil.' On top of the subscription, creating a sandbox needs a role assignment: 'To manage and create sandboxes, you need the Azure role Container Apps SandboxGroup Data Owner.' Country limit, quoted: 'If your country is not listed, the offer is not available in your region.'

confidence_note: the sandboxes overview was read on 2026-10-22. It establishes the lifecycle and the stop-billing behaviour and does not publish a free allowance, so the requirement below is the Container Apps consumption allowance the same vendor prices on its pricing page, not a sandbox-specific grant

evidence.proved: 'Sandboxes are provisioned from prewarmed pools for near-instant availability' and 'You pay no CPU or memory fees when sandboxes are stopped' and 'Suspend and resume: Snapshot full state including memory and disk, and resume later with sub-second restore times', quoted
the Azure subscription that bills sandbox compute takes a phone number and a credit or non-prepaid debit card at signup
